sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: The common fig is a large deciduous shrub or small tree, often 5–9 m tall and spreading. Native to the Mediterranean region and western Asia, it is widely cultivated.

sections.title: Leaves and figs
sections.text: Its large leaves are lobed. The many tiny flowers are hidden inside a hollow receptacle, the syconium, which develops into the fleshy 1.5–5 cm fig.

sections.title: Edibility and caution
sections.text: Ripe figs are edible. Latex from stems and unripe fruit can irritate skin and eyes.
